items.summary: Rather than racing to replace people, we should build AI tools that amplify human expertise and expand opportunity.

items.summary: A pair of massive shield volcanoes have been pinpointed by lunar spacecraft.

items.title: To shield the fetus, link a protein to these drugs
items.summary: Adding albumin to popular antibody-based medicines helps to block their passage through the placenta.

items.title: Astronaut vest cuts radiation exposure in half
items.summary: Tests on uncrewed NASA mission showed garment could spare astronauts the worst effects of solar storms.

items.title: These trees are making air quality in cities worse
items.summary: They release compounds that contribute to ozone emissions, and rising temperatures could exacerbate the problem.

items.title: Exclusive: NSF set to issue lowest number of new grants in four decades
items.summary: The US science-funding agency is withholding $1 billion of its budget so that the money can go to a special White House project.

items.title: Moderna cancer vaccine stops melanoma returning: what’s next for personalized treatments?
items.summary: Promising trial results suggest cancer vaccines work and could be used to target other tumours.

items.title: Investors’ sneak peak: can this AI tool spot the science that will lead to patents?
items.summary: The approach could speed up investment decisions, but researchers say it has flaws.

items.title: Staggering 90% of biomedical papers now show signs of AI help
items.summary: The figure, which is much higher than previous estimates of Large Language Model use, is for papers published in December and archived in PubMed

items.title: Researcher, heal thyself: meet the scientists studying their own diseases
items.summary: Studying a condition after being diagnosed with it can be rewarding but also presents some ethical and psychological challenges.

items.title: Too much mate choice overwhelms frogs
items.summary: Female treefrogs select less carefully when hearing a chorus of males.

items.summary: Star orbiting close to Sagittarius A* could reveal its spin — plus, how exoskeletons might change the way humans move.

items.title: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance
items.summary: Functional lymphoid structures within the skull bone marrow enable central nervous system immunosurveillance and shape immune responses to brain disease.

items.title: Observation of conformal field theory spectra in a quantum simulator
items.summary: Measurements on an array of optically trapped neutral atoms at a quantum phase transition provide a direct observation of the universal excitation spectrum predicted by conformal field theory.

items.title: Wake-activated neuronal populations that regulate sleep drive
items.summary: Whole-brain activity mapping, targeted cell manipulations and electrophysiology in mice identify wake-activated neuronal populations that are crucial for sleep drive and can persistently reduce daily sleep amount.

items.title: Increasing CO<sub>2</sub> levels fertilize C<sub>4</sub> grass production
items.summary: By combining a meta-analysis of CO2 enrichment experiments with three decades of southern African savanna observations, an increase in biomass production by C4 grasses under rising CO2 levels in water-limited environments is revealed.

items.title: A global atmospheric methane record from a tropical ice core
items.summary: A 2,000-year Peruvian ice core record of atmospheric CH4 concentrations contains the first historical global CH4 record from the low latitudes, and implementation of a four-box model indicates higher equatorial CH4 strength than previous estimates from polar-only records.

items.title: Family genetic designs in MoBa provide insights into health and functioning
items.summary: The Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study demonstrates how family-based genomic data can disentangle direct genetic effects from confounding, improving studies of health and human development.

items.title: Asymmetric prefrontal representations for leader–follower dynamics
items.summary: Mice spontaneously form leader and follower roles during cooperation, and the medial prefrontal cortex encodes these role dynamics and an egocentric social value map of the partner’s position.

items.title: Atomic-scale double-slit interferometry with a focused electron probe
items.summary: Double-slit interferometry at the atomic scale is demonstrated using scanning transmission electron microscopy to provide evidence of interference fringes generated with a focused electron beam encountering two silicon atomic columns separated by 1.36 Å.

items.title: Synthesis of pyrroles from isoxazoles by an O-to-C skeletal edit
items.summary: A one-pot skeletal-editing reaction replaces isoxazole oxygen with carbon to form challenging pyrroles, enabled by an N-propargylic enaminone intermediate and a computational model predicting reaction outcomes.

items.title: Human brain organoids record the passage of time over multiple years
items.summary: Human brain organoids were developed for over five years in culture to demonstrate that brain cells can continue to mature and record the passage of time, following human-specific endogenous programs, even outside the context of the organism.

items.title: Multiyear tropical warm pool warming drives slowdown in Antarctic mass loss
items.summary: Recent Antarctic ice mass gain was linked to a recurrent atmospheric teleconnection, but this recurs about once per decade in observations and historical simulations so does not yet reflect a global-warming-driven moistening of Antarctica.

items.title: The HydroGym reinforcement learning platform for fluid dynamics
items.summary: HydroGym offers over 60 standardized reinforcement-learning flow-control environments and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to a 3D wing, cutting local skin friction by 38% and exploration costs by four orders of magnitude.

items.title: An Icelandic pangenome reference
items.summary: Newly developed methods enable construction of Icelandic haplotypes and mapping of population-scale short reads to a pangenome by reducing reference bias and improving discovery in low-mappability regions, revealing many novel variants, including pathogenic alleles.

items.title: Psychedelics align brain activity with context
items.summary: The psychedelic psilocybin reorganizes brain activity into structured, context-aligned patterns that integrate internal and external processing, providing a neural basis for the felt continuity between self and world, elucidating how the psychedelic state translates into psychological change.

items.title: Discovery of a star sensitive to the spin of Sagittarius A*
items.summary: The discovery of the fast-orbiting star S301 near Sagittarius A* offers a promising new probe of the central black hole spin of the Milky Way through relativistic orbit measurements.

items.title: Safety and security of large language models in healthcare
items.summary: The Review examines rapid LLM adoption in clinical care, outlining emerging security and safety risks across development stages, key protective layers, clinically relevant threats and current mitigation responsibilities in a single integrated framework.

items.title: Pervasive phosphorylation by phage T7 kinase disarms bacterial defences
items.summary: The T7 bacteriophage deactivates bacterial defence systems through T7K phosphorylation of nearly all host and phage proteins during infection.

items.title: A biased allosteric modulator is a molecular glue for β<sub>2</sub>AR dimerization
items.summary: AP-7-168, an optimized derivative of a β-arrestin-biased negative allosteric modulator of the β2-adrenergic receptor (β2AR), functions as a molecular glue to stabilize β2AR homodimerization.

items.title: Twenty-two easy ways to power up your lab meetings
items.summary: Scientists share help and advice on how they got their research discussions flowing.

items.title: Virus deploys a ‘loose cannon’ enzyme to overpower bacterial defences
items.summary: Viruses that infect bacteria must either evade or counter the defence systems of their host. The viral kinase enzyme T7K has been found to phosphorylate nearly all bacterial proteins, but its specificity for DNA-binding proteins enables it to disable defence systems that target nucleic acids.

items.title: South Africa’s scientists must register with official body or risk prison, according to draft law
items.summary: Many researchers are unaware of an upcoming law that will require them to register with a regulatory body, as is the case for engineers and health-care professionals.

items.title: How do people live beyond 110? Abundance of cancer-killing cells might be key
items.summary: Research on people 110 years and older reveals an immune system that continues to adapt.

items.title: Psychedelics tune the brain to the environment
items.summary: Rather than just scrambling neural activity, the psychedelic substance psilocybin also reorganizes brain dynamics so as to align with a person’s context and experiences.

items.title: Screening babies’ genomes could save lives. Here’s how it would work
items.summary: Massive genomic newborn-screening studies are under way all over the globe. But questions about scalability, feasibility and net benefit remain.

items.title: Rudolph A. Marcus obituary: theoretical chemist who explained how electrons jump between molecules
items.summary: His calculations explain the efficiency of batteries and solar cells.

items.title: AI tool lets researchers ‘vibe code’ in the quantum realm
items.summary: An autonomous AI agent can write and execute quantum computing code, but it sometimes needs a human touch.

items.title: Computational ‘gym’ trains AI models to control turbulence
items.summary: The HydroGym computational environment teaches agents strategies for fluid-flow control that can be applied to scenarios they have not encountered before.

items.title: Delisted
items.summary: Called to account.

items.title: Human organoids that mimic brain development grown for years in lab
items.summary: Models of how the brain changes over time could help researchers to understand how diseases affect the organ later in life.

items.title: Activity of solar-driven polymer catalysts unleashed to produce a potential green fuel
items.summary: Engineering of polymer crystals has vastly increased the activity of these materials as catalysts for producing hydrogen fuel from water, using only sunlight.

items.title: The Antarctic ice sheet has gained mass — but probably not for long
items.summary: Since 2020, snowfall has largely counterbalanced the melting of the Antarctic ice sheet. The atmospheric effect that causes this has been identified — and it’s temporary.

items.title: Daily briefing: How 3D printers are changing lab work
items.summary: Printing custom lab tools can be cheaper than buying them. Plus, South African scientists might soon have to register with a regulatory body and what an exoskeleton-powered future might look like.
